content: If the antimicrobial compound reaches the necessary concentration at the site of infection, it can inhibit the growth of the pathogen. A result classified as Intermediate suggests that the outcome is equivocal. In cases where the microorganism is not fully susceptible to alternative, clinically feasible drugs, the test should be repeated. This category indicates potential clinical applicability in body sites where the drug is physiologically concentrated. It also provides a buffer zone to account for minor uncontrolled technical factors that could otherwise lead to significant discrepancies in interpretation. A result classified as Resistant indicates that the antimicrobial is unlikely to inhibit the growth of the pathogen at concentrations typically achievable at the infection site. In such cases, alternative therapy should be selected. Standard nitrofurantoin powder should yield the specified minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) values. For the diffusion technique using the 300-mcg nitrofurantoin disk, the provided criteria should be met. Chronic rodent bioassays conducted in male and female Sprague-Dawley rats over 75 weeks, as well as in Swiss mice and BDF1 mice, showed no evidence of carcinogenicity. However, nitrofurantoin demonstrated carcinogenic activity in female B6C3F1 mice, as evidenced by increased incidences of tubular adenomas, benign mixed tumors, and granulosa cell tumors of the ovary. In male F344/N rats, there were increased incidences of rare kidney tubular cell neoplasms, bone osteosarcomas, and subcutaneous tissue neoplasms. In one study involving subcutaneous administration of 75 mg/kg nitrofurantoin to pregnant female mice, lung papillary adenomas of unknown significance were observed in the F1 generation. Nitrofurantoin has been shown to induce point mutations in certain strains of Salmonella typhimurium and forward mutations in L5178Y mouse lymphoma cells. It also caused increased numbers of sister chromatid exchanges and chromosomal aberrations in Chinese hamster ovary cells, but not in human cells in culture. Results of the sex-linked recessive lethal assay in Drosophila were negative following administration of nitrofurantoin by feeding or injection. Nitrofurantoin did not induce heritable mutations in the rodent models examined. The clinical significance of the findings related to carcinogenicity and mutagenicity in the context of nitrofurantoin's therapeutic use in humans remains unknown. Administration of high doses of nitrofurantoin to rats caused temporary spermatogenic arrest, which was reversible upon discontinuation of the drug. Doses of 10 mg/kg/day or greater in healthy human males may, in certain unpredictable cases, result in slight to moderate spermatogenic arrest with a decrease in sperm count. Clinical Studies There is limited information available regarding clinical studies of nitrofurantoin in the drug label. How Supplied Furadantin Oral Suspension is available in a glass amber bottle containing 230 mL (NDC 59630-450-08). Storage Avoid exposure to strong light, as it may darken the drug. The suspension is stable when stored between 20°C and 25°C (68°F to 77°F), with permissible excursions to 15°C–30°C (59°F–86°F). Protect from freezing. Shake vigorously before use. Dispense in a tight, light-resistant plastic (PET) or glass container. Use within 30 days. Keep out of reach of children. Prescription only. Patient Counseling Information Patients should be advised to take Furadantin with food to enhance tolerance and improve drug absorption. They should complete the full course of therapy but contact their physician if any unusual symptoms occur during treatment. Diarrhea is a common side effect of antibiotics and usually resolves after discontinuation of the antibiotic. However, if watery and bloody stools (with or without stomach cramps and fever) develop, even as late as two or more months after the last dose, patients should contact their physician immediately. Patients should also be advised not to use antacid preparations containing magnesium trisilicate while taking Furadantin. Precautions with Alcohol The interaction between alcohol and nitrofurantoin has not been established. Patients should consult their doctor regarding the effects of consuming alcohol while on this medication.
